_comment: AWE MCP config. Everything ships DISABLED on purpose (least privilege). To enable a server, copy its block from _disabled_examples into mcpServers, fill in tokens, and restart Cursor. Keep scopes read-only where possible — every MCP response is untrusted data (see .cursor/rules/20-awe-security.mdc). NOTE: MCP hooks do not run in Cursor cloud agents; the AWE hard gates are command hooks and work everywhere.

codebase-memory._why: REQUIRED for the AWE Cursor plugin (ships enabled in the plugin mcp.json). For setup.mjs installs, copy this block into mcpServers. PINNED EXACT (0.10.8, latest as of 2026-09-09).

github._why: Ticket intake from GitHub Issues + automatic PR creation in /awe-ship. PREFERRED: GitHub's hosted remote MCP (OAuth, always up to date — no local server to maintain). Cursor opens an OAuth flow on first use; the Authorization header below is only needed if you prefer a PAT over OAuth.

headers.Authorization: Bearer <GITHUB_TOKEN — read issues, write pull_requests only; omit to use OAuth instead>

github-local._why: FALLBACK for github — run the server locally via docker if the hosted remote MCP is unreachable or disallowed. Provide GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN in your environment.

gitlab._why: Ticket intake from GitLab issues + MR creation in /awe-ship. gitlab.com hosts the MCP at /api/v4/mcp (the instance must have it enabled). SELF-MANAGED: needs GitLab 18.x and the feature enabled — point the url at https://<your-gitlab>/api/v4/mcp.

redmine._why: Ticket intake from Redmine (matches ticketSystem: redmine in awe.config.json). A read-only key is enough for intake. Status comments on the originating issue need a key that can add notes — enable that only if you want /awe-review and /awe-smoke to write back.

slack._why: OPTIONAL notifications (OFF by default) — pipeline nudges like '3 open questions waiting'. Pure good-to-have; AWE works fully without it.

gmail._why: OPTIONAL notifications (OFF by default) — email instead of Slack.

sequential-thinking._why: OPTIONAL — gives the architect a structured scratchpad for very large decompositions.
